messages:
jin: FYI ran an inter-region eviction risk sim for EU->US failover during peak. results look concerning, hitting 78% GPU concurrency in us-west within 6m :grimacing:

mira: can you paste the sim command + parameters?

jin: 
```
./evict-sim --src-region=eu-west --dst-region=us-west --traffic=seasonal_peak --duration=3600 --model-mix="mixA:0.6,mixB:0.4" --cold-start-penalty=0.85
```

liam: output snapshot:
```
time,src_used,dst_used,dst_headroom
0,0.62,0.58,0.42
360,0.64,0.78,0.22  # danger zone
1200,0.66,0.85,0.15  # eviction likely
```

ops-bot: ALERT: us-west GPU pool > 80% for 3m, auto-scale triggered :rotating_light:

sam: mitigation options - (1) pre-warm 8 GPUs in us-west (2) route 20% traffic to dedicated fallback models (3) throttle low-priority requests. cost tradeoffs? :money_with_wings:

anna: quick cost calc: pre-warm 8xA100 ~ $2.3k/day. Routing to fallback reduces token throughput by ~15% but saves ~$1.8k/day. throttling saves latency-sensitive SLAs.

jin: agree. prefer (2)+(3) short term. can we add conditional pre-warm only if sim predicts >75% in next 10m? liam, can you add that to the sim and run across APAC/EU/US?

liam: will do. adding predictive prewarm flag to simulator. pushing branch: https://git.redwood/infrasim/evict-sim/predictive-prewarm :thumbsup:

mira: add a dashboard panel for projected headroom in next 15m, include tokens/sec and concurrent reqs. I'll own the dashboard.

jin: assign follow-ups: liam -> updated sim + runs across regions, mira -> dashboard, anna -> final cost estimate for exec. check back EOD. :white_check_mark:
